LESSON: TIME

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.6: Time
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we estimate time?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Work with peers in reading and tell time in a.m. And p.m. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers or teacher to perform the task.

2. Use digital and analogue clocks. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC (residual speech/ digital

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Work with peers in reading and tell time in a.m. And p.m. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, appropriate assistive devices or be assisted by peers or teacher to perform the task.
2. Use digital and analogue clocks. Those with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC (residual speech/ digital

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Imagination and creativity: learner explores new ways of estimating time using shadows of objects within

the environment.

• Digital literacy: learner discusses collaboratively with others and records time using digital devices.

Values:
Integrity: learner consistently measures and records accurately the duration of events in hours and minutes

using digital or analogue clocks.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Learner adheres to simple safety rules when telling and recording time using electronic clock to enhance safety

and security.

Link to other subjects

Learner relates estimation of time of the day to weather and climate in Social Studies.
